claims.text: The owner's co-founder came back from a conference with ten hard questions, the ones people actually ask about a product like RiskMandate.
claims.quote: My co-founder came back from a conference with ten hard questions, the ones people actually ask about a product like RiskMandate.

claims.text: RiskMandate defines the risk that comes with the mandate a business gives an agent.
claims.quote: RiskMandate defines the risk that comes with the mandate a business gives an agent.

claims.text: An Agent Behaviour Policy is a written description, for one agent in one deployment, of four things: mandate, grant, delta and barriers.
claims.quote: a written description, for one agent in one deployment, of four things.

claims.text: The delta, or gap, is reach minus mandate: excess, unbounded excess, shortfall; it is derived, never authored.
claims.quote: Reach minus mandate: excess, unbounded excess, shortfall

claims.text: Barriers are recorded as none, expectation, setting or boundary, and only a boundary is a control.
claims.quote: Recorded as none, expectation, setting or boundary; only a boundary is a control

claims.text: The goal of every engagement is the smallest mandate, the smallest reach, the smallest gap, and the smallest residual where the agent has to police itself.
claims.quote: The goal of every engagement is the smallest mandate, the smallest reach, the smallest gap, and the smallest residual where the agent has to police itself.

claims.text: RiskMandate is not in the request path, by design; being inline would make it a competitor to everyone and put liability on it.
claims.quote: RiskMandate is not in the request path, by design.

claims.text: A $75k order is only possible if the reach allowed it on day one; the policy surfaces that as unbounded excess before any action.
claims.quote: A $75k order is only possible if the reach allowed it on day one

claims.text: An agent permitted £10k per action that can perform a thousand actions carries a £10m exposure, so unbounded includes volume, not just size.
claims.quote: An agent permitted £10k per action that can perform a thousand actions carries a £10m exposure.

value.unit: million GBP exposure from £10k per action over a thousand actions

claims.text: Self-policing is not the goal but the fallback; the value is in creating the policy, which discovers what is possible and where the gaps are.
claims.quote: Self-policing is not the goal; it is the fallback.

claims.text: Claude has flagged its own actions as outside the policy, which improves the policy, but that is the agent checking itself, not RiskMandate watching.
claims.quote: Claude has flagged its own actions as outside the policy, and that improves the policy.

claims.text: Reach is a computed value, and new capability can only ever land in the reach as excess, never as new authority, because the mandate is locked business logic.
claims.quote: so new capability can only ever land as excess, never as new authority.

claims.text: When the reach calculation is wired to the pipeline, a change recomputes the delta, triggers a re-review, re-evaluates the licence to operate and escalates up to pulling the plug.
claims.quote: escalation follows, up to automatic loss of the licence, which means pulling the plug.

claims.text: Connect Gmail to several agents and every agent inherits everything the connection allows; in the owner's own setup, an inbox agent and a briefing agent can both send email.
claims.quote: Connect Gmail to several agents and every agent inherits everything the connection allows.

claims.text: Everything RiskMandate builds is open source, policies, code, vaults and backend, with no proprietary layer; the customer buys time, maintenance and de-risking of change.
claims.quote: Everything we build is open source: policies, code, vaults, backend. There is no proprietary layer.

claims.text: The four one-off levels, pack, vault, corrected and signed, are currently £10, £50, £500 and £1,500 per agent per deployment.
claims.quote: currently £10, £50, £500 and £1,500 per agent per deployment

value.unit: GBP, the top one-off level per agent per deployment

claims.text: Above the levels sit £5k, £50k and £100k engagements, sized by resources consumed, customisation and support.
claims.quote: Above them sit £5k, £50k and £100k engagements, sized by resources consumed, customisation and support.

claims.text: The four levels exist, two have never sold, payment rails are incomplete, and design partners are currently free.
claims.quote: The four levels exist, two have never sold, payment rails are incomplete, and design partners are currently free

claims.text: Liability always sits with the customer; the moment of authorisation is the grant, not the mandate, and exposure exists the instant the grant exists.
claims.quote: Liability always sits with the customer. The moment of authorisation is the grant, not the mandate.

claims.text: No risk transfer exists today; the honest claim is that RiskMandate makes agents insurable, it does not insure them.
claims.quote: No risk transfer exists today. The honest claim: we make agents insurable.

claims.text: RiskMandate is not an insurer: it carries no risk and places no cover.
claims.quote: Not an insurer. We carry no risk and place no cover.

claims.text: RiskMandate is not a one-button solution, because what can stop an agent depends on what exists in each deployment.
claims.quote: Not a one-button solution. What can actually stop an agent depends on what exists in each deployment.

claims.text: RiskMandate is an enabler of the other vendors, not a competitor; every written rule gives an existing product something to enforce and a number to move.
claims.quote: RiskMandate is an enabler of the other vendors, not a competitor.

claims.text: The moat is method, trust and maintenance on an open-source base: a services-and-expertise moat rather than a product artefact.
claims.quote: The moat is method, trust and maintenance on an open-source base: a services-and-expertise moat rather than a product artefact.

claims.text: RiskMandate has proposed Agent Behaviour Policies as an OWASP project, because platforms adopting them makes the approach the standard.
claims.quote: which is why we have proposed Agent Behaviour Policies as an OWASP project.

claims.text: The supply chain is just a bigger agent: a compromised dependency is a grant that exploded or a boundary that vanished, which recomputes the delta like any other change.
claims.quote: The supply chain is just a bigger agent.

claims.text: Trust travels through connectivity in the graph: trust in a situation grows with independent, corroborating signals.
claims.quote: Trust in a situation grows with independent, corroborating signals.

claims.text: RiskMandate authors the policy, shares the decision as a design-time pre-commitment, and never enforces; monitoring is the customer's.
claims.quote: RiskMandate authors, shares the decision as a design-time pre-commitment, and never enforces.

claims.text: Reversal is the next evolution of the policy, built on digital twins, replay and version control, and bounded by one-way doors.
claims.quote: Reversal is the next evolution, built on digital twins, replay and version control, and bounded by one-way doors.

claims.text: Attenuating delegated authority between agents needs PKI on top of the policy: authorisation by encryption, not by privilege.
claims.quote: Attenuating delegated authority needs PKI on top: authorisation by encryption, not by privilege.

claims.text: The headline metric is reduction in the risk the business has to accept; every time a grant shrinks, the gap and the risk shrink.
claims.quote: The headline metric is reduction in accepted risk.

claims.text: RiskMandate owns the risk and coverage metrics and explicitly does not own runtime metrics such as latency, false positives or time to recover.
claims.quote: RiskMandate owns the risk and coverage metrics, and explicitly does not own runtime metrics such as latency or time to recover.

claims.text: Three things on riskmandate.ai contradict the position above and were still there when the page was written on 9 October 2026.
claims.quote: Three things on riskmandate.ai contradict the position above, and were still there when this page was written on 9 October 2026

claims.text: The Level 1 price is £10 on the home and pricing pages and £5 on the Licence to Operate page; one of them is wrong.
claims.quote: £10 on the home and pricing pages, £5 on the Licence to Operate page. One of them is wrong.

value.unit: GBP, Level 1 price on the home page, against £5 elsewhere

claims.text: The 0.388 reproduction precision figure is quoted from the interview; its source page was not located while preparing the article.
claims.quote: The 0.388 figure is quoted from the interview; its source page was not located while preparing this one.
